likely_redundant_clusters.reason: Same FIFO request order; differences are mostly placement policy.
All encode short-work preference; they differ in prompt/output weighting, priority, and KV block handling.
All approximate prefill budget or long-prompt throttling without true chunk-size actions.
All use KV feasibility/pressure for placement or admission, though kv_constrained_online adds urgency-aware admission.

candidate_parent_sets.why: Combines short-work throughput, SLO/load admission, and prefill pressure control.
Combines WSP efficiency with KV reserve protection and starvation control.
Combines service-time ranking, overload throttling, and class-level fairness.

coverage_interpretation.current_library_shape: Several distinct behavioral families are present, but many policies are monolithic and expose direct actions rather than reusable modules.
coverage_interpretation.basis_assessment: Approximate behavioral basis for admission plus ranking plus placement exists for the current monolithic simulator. It is not a full basis for cache-aware, disaggregated, splitting, or heterogeneous routing policies.
coverage_interpretation.composition_value_hypothesis: Most plausible near-term gain is not arbitrary policy mixing; it is component-wise recombination of WSP priority, SCORPIO admission, KV guard, prefill/phase guard, and aging/fairness safeguards.
